- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast lows.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment = 1.00), especially in 30-day horizon; apply downward correction of 3–8% for such cases.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion correction: forecast = 0.8×previous forecast + 0.2×new sentiment-weighted average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment volatility; smooth 30d forecast by averaging with 18d historical mean if sentiment is erratic.
- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over 5+ days, model often overestimates 30d price; apply 3–7% downward adjustment to avoid “sentiment inflation”.
- If true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 5 days of forecast, assume model is “overconfident” and reduce subsequent forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence.
